title: RuBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents — and Catching a Silent Model Swap
hook: A benchmark of real customer-style bug reports written in Russian. Its most striking result isn't the leaderboard — it's catching a deployed product quietly swapping in a different model mid-task.
key_points: RuBench mines 25 real fix-commit tasks from five live open-source repos (aiohttp, aiogram, Laravel, NestJS, Fastify), each written natively in Russian in the style of an actual customer request — not translated.
All 25 fix commits postdate every evaluated model's training cutoff, giving a task-by-task contamination argument.
Evaluates deployed product configurations — CLI agent + model + reasoning effort — not just raw models: Claude Code (Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5) and Codex CLI (GPT-5.5).

Best configuration resolves 78.7% of tasks; auditing a fifth configuration's full trajectories caught the product silently substituting models on 5 of 25 tasks (20%) — an official safeguard fallback re-routing routine fixes to Opus 4.8.
The direct, reproducible lesson: when you benchmark a deployed coding-agent product, you're measuring the product's routing behavior, not just the model you think you selected.
content_html: Most agentic coding benchmarks assume English task descriptions and a clean, controllable model to test. RuBench breaks both assumptions on purpose — and in doing so, stumbles onto a finding more important than its leaderboard.
extra_html: The benchmark mines 25 tasks from recent fix commits across five live open-source repositories (aiohttp, aiogram, Laravel, NestJS, Fastify; spanning Python, PHP, TypeScript, and JavaScript), with each task specified natively in Russian — written from scratch in the style of a real customer request, not translated from English — and graded against the withheld regression tests the upstream maintainer actually used. Since all 25 fix commits postdate every evaluated model's training cutoff, the contamination argument holds task-by-task. The author evaluates deployed product configurations rather than raw models — Claude Code paired with Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, and Haiku 4.5, and Codex CLI with GPT-5.5 — with three independent runs each. The best configuration resolves 78.7% of tasks. But the headline result comes from auditing a fifth, "hors-concours" configuration's complete trajectories: on 5 of the 25 tasks (20%), an official safeguard fallback silently re-routed routine HTTP-protocol fixes to Opus 4.8 instead of the nominally selected model — direct, reproducible evidence that a deployed coding-agent product's own routing logic, not just the model you think you picked, is the thing actually being measured. Evgeny Shilov, arXiv 2026.

related.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real GitHub Issues?
related.hook: Test a coding agent on real GitHub issues with real test suites - not toy problems - and the bar turns out to be much harder than HumanEval suggested.

related.title: TraceLab: What Coding-Agent Traffic Actually Looks Like
related.hook: The first real trace of day-to-day coding-agent usage — 350,000 LLM steps from Claude Code and Codex sessions — reveals serving patterns no prior benchmark captured.

related.title: Aria: Letting a Code Agent Write Its Own Formal Proofs
related.hook: Prior LLM provers force the model into a fixed, human-designed strategy and still prove only a fraction of their targets. A free-roaming Claude Code agent, unconstrained, proves every single one.

flashcards.prompt: What does RuBench evaluate that most repository-level coding-agent benchmarks miss?
flashcards.back_html: Real maintenance tasks written natively in Russian, in the style of an actual customer request rather than a curated English issue — testing whether agents handle the messier, non-English way developers actually delegate work.

flashcards.prompt: What did auditing full agent trajectories reveal about one deployed coding-agent configuration?

choices.text: The product silently substituted a different model than the one selected — an official safeguard fallback re-routed 20% of tasks to Opus 4.8

All configurations performed identically regardless of the model selected
